sentences.en: Hey, I'm Benjamin Poulin and I'm Mark Ronson and welcome to The Reframers, a podcast that's all about the love of design and the culture that surrounds it.
sentences.zh: 大家好，我是本杰明·普兰，我是马克·荣森，欢迎收听《重构者》，这是一档专注于设计之美及其背后文化的播客。

sentences.en: Even back when I was DJing in nightclubs in the era of vinyl,
sentences.zh: 即使是在我还在夜店当DJ的黑胶唱片时代，

sentences.en: every night you took 300 of your most prized possessions to work with you and you turned a DJ booth into this like living pop-up museum of beautiful 50-year-old artifacts.
sentences.zh: 你每天晚上都要带上300件你最珍视的宝贝去工作，把DJ台变成一个充满50年历史精美文物的流动博物馆。

sentences.en: Listen to The Reframers from Audemars Piguet now on your favorite podcast platforMs.
sentences.zh: 现在就在你喜欢的播客平台上收听爱彼出品的《重构者》。

sentences.en: From The New York Times, I'm Michael Barbaro.
sentences.zh: 我是《纽约时报》的迈克尔·巴尔巴罗。

sentences.en: This is The Daily.
sentences.zh: 这是《每日新闻》。

sentences.en: Today, the Justice Department appoints a special counsel to investigate the president's ties to Russia.
sentences.zh: 今天，司法部任命了一位特别检察官，负责调查总统与俄罗斯之间的联系。

sentences.en: After months of trying to influence that investigation, has Trump just lost control of it?
sentences.zh: 在试图影响这项调查数月之后，特朗普是否已经失去了对调查的控制？

sentences.en: And Rod Rosenstein, the man who picked the special counsel, is he the president's problem or his protector?
sentences.zh: 而挑选这位特别检察官的罗德·罗森斯坦，他到底是总统的麻烦，还是总统的保护伞？

sentences.en: It's Thursday, May 18.
sentences.zh: 今天是5月18日，星期四。

sentences.en: Shortly after the Justice Department named a special counsel on Wednesday night, I called Matt Apuzzo.
sentences.zh: 周三晚上司法部宣布任命特别检察官后不久，我给马特·阿普佐打了电话。

sentences.en: I'll talk to you later.
sentences.zh: 我待会儿再跟你聊。

sentences.en: I've got to jump on this other call.
sentences.zh: 我得去接另一个电话。

sentences.en: All right, bye.
sentences.zh: 好的，再见。

sentences.en: Hey, what's going on?
sentences.zh: 嘿，怎么了？

sentences.en: Hey, Apuzzo.
sentences.zh: 嘿，阿普佐。

sentences.en: It's Barbara.
sentences.zh: 我是芭芭拉。

sentences.en: Of course it's you.
sentences.zh: 我就知道是你。

sentences.en: Are we in the middle of breaking news and are you calling me?
sentences.zh: 我们正处于突发新闻的中心，你却在给我打电话？

sentences.en: Yes, yes.
sentences.zh: 没错，没错。

sentences.en: Matt, what exactly is a special counsel?
sentences.zh: 马特，特别检察官到底是什么？

sentences.en: Well, that's been picked because the public is concerned that there are questions about the Justice Department's independence.
sentences.zh: 嗯，之所以选择他，是因为公众担心司法部的独立性存在问题。

sentences.en: It's somebody who can lead an investigation while giving people confidence that this thing's going to be done independently.
sentences.zh: 他是一个能够领导调查，同时让人们相信调查会独立进行的人。

sentences.en: It's going to be done appropriately and nobody's going to mess around with it.
sentences.zh: 调查会以恰当的方式进行，没有人会从中作梗。

sentences.en: And what are the powers, traditionally, of a special counsel?
sentences.zh: 那么，特别检察官通常拥有什么权力？

sentences.en: Well, a special counsel can do anything that a federal prosecutor can do.
sentences.zh: 嗯，特别检察官可以做任何联邦检察官能做的事。

sentences.en: They can subpoena people.
sentences.zh: 他们可以传唤证人。

sentences.en: They can haul people for a grand jury.
sentences.zh: 他们可以传唤人员出席大陪审团会议。

sentences.en: They can subpoena documents.
sentences.zh: 他们可以传唤文件。

sentences.en: And in this case, what the Justice Department is doing is basically saying we need somebody who's independent from the Trump administration who can come in, run this investigation,
sentences.zh: 在这种情况下，司法部的做法基本上是说，我们需要一个独立于特朗普政府的人进来，负责这项调查，

sentences.en: and give the public confidence that it's going to be done thoroughly.
sentences.zh: 并让公众相信调查会彻底进行。

sentences.en: It's going to be insulated from even the perception of pressure from the White House or anybody else in the Trump administration.
sentences.zh: 它将不受白宫或特朗普政府中任何其他人施加压力的影响，甚至连这种感觉都不会有。

sentences.en: And so what is happening here is you're getting a special prosecutor who, while in the hierarchy, is answerable up to the deputy attorney general,
sentences.zh: 所以现在发生的情况是，你得到了一位特别检察官，虽然在层级上他要向副司法部长汇报，

sentences.en: is really going to be allowed to run the investigation and serve as the guy running the case.
sentences.zh: 但他确实会被允许独立开展调查，并作为案件的负责人。

sentences.en: And just to be really clear about this, a special counsel is still in some ways answerable to the Department of Justice and therefore to the president of the United States.
sentences.zh: 为了说得更清楚一点，特别检察官在某些方面仍然要对司法部负责，因此也要对美国总统负责。

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: And I'm sure there's going to be a lot of political hand-rigging over that very issue because it's not an entirely autonomous position.
sentences.zh: 我相信围绕这个问题肯定会有很多政治上的博弈，因为它并不是一个完全自治的职位。

sentences.en: Matt, why has there been such resistance in Washington to doing this very thing, appointing a special counsel until now?
sentences.zh: 马特，为什么华盛顿一直以来对任命特别检察官这件事如此抵触？

sentences.en: Why did it take so long, do you think?
sentences.zh: 你认为为什么花了这么长时间？

sentences.en: Well, Republicans, of course, were loathe to do it because it elevates this, right?
sentences.zh: 嗯，共和党人当然不愿意这样做，因为这会提升事件的级别，对吧？

sentences.en: I mean, it basically says this is a big deal.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，这基本上是在说这是一件大事。

sentences.en: I think the feeling at the White House, and they've said it over and over again, that there's no there there, so we don't need a special prosecutor.
sentences.zh: 我认为白宫的感觉，而且他们已经反复说过，那里什么都没有，所以我们不需要特别检察官。

sentences.en: Congress can investigate it.
sentences.zh: 国会可以调查它。

sentences.en: And we have a deputy attorney general who is regarded as an independent straight shooter who can lead the just-farm investigation.
sentences.zh: 而且我们有一位被视为独立、直率的副司法部长，他可以领导这项调查。

sentences.en: So there's no real need.
sentences.zh: 所以没有真正的必要。

sentences.en: What do we think changed?
sentences.zh: 我们认为是什么改变了局面？

sentences.en: Why now is there a special counsel?
sentences.zh: 为什么现在有了特别检察官？

sentences.en: Well, we're still reporting this out, obviously, but the two big things that changed were the president fired Jim Comey, relying, he said originally,
sentences.zh: 嗯，我们显然还在对此进行报道，但改变的两大关键点是，总统解雇了吉姆·科米，他最初声称，

sentences.en: on the advice of the deputy attorney general, Rod Rosenstein, who was leading the Russia investigation.
sentences.zh: 是基于负责俄罗斯调查的副司法部长罗德·罗森斯坦的建议。

sentences.en: And then, like, the next day, the president said, oh, I was going to do that anyways, and while I was firing the FBI director, I was, in fact,
sentences.zh: 然后，第二天，总统就说，哦，我反正都要这么做，而且我在解雇联邦调查局局长的时候，实际上，

sentences.en: thinking about how dumb this Russia investigation was.
sentences.zh: 就在想这项俄罗斯调查有多愚蠢。

sentences.en: There was nothing there.
sentences.zh: 那里什么都没有。

sentences.en: And so if you put those two together,
sentences.zh: 所以如果你把这两件事放在一起看，

sentences.en: it says the president fired the FBI director while thinking about the Russia investigation and relied on the memo written by the guy supervising the Russia investigation.
sentences.zh: 就说明总统是在考虑俄罗斯调查的同时解雇了联邦调查局局长，并且依赖了由负责俄罗斯调查的人所写的备忘录。

sentences.en: So that's the first thing.
sentences.zh: 所以这是第一点。

sentences.en: And then the second thing is the news that Mike Schmidt, our incredible colleague, wrote about how there are these memos that detail conversations between Jim Comey,
sentences.zh: 第二点是我们的杰出同事迈克·施密特报道的消息，关于那些详细记录了吉姆·科米，

sentences.en: the FBI director, and President Trump, in which it appears that the president was telling Comey that he should shut down, you know, one aspect of this investigation.
sentences.zh: 也就是联邦调查局局长，与特朗普总统之间谈话的备忘录，其中似乎显示总统告诉科米，他应该停止这项调查的某个方面。

sentences.en: So once those came out, I mean, I think the die was probably caSt.
sentences.zh: 所以一旦这些消息传出来，我想大局可能已定。

sentences.en: So let's talk about the man chosen for this job of special counsel.
sentences.zh: 那么我们来谈谈被选中担任特别检察官的这个人。

sentences.en: What should we know about Robert Mueller?
sentences.zh: 关于罗伯特·穆勒，我们应该了解些什么？

sentences.en: Former FBI director.
sentences.zh: 前联邦调查局局长。

sentences.en: He served a full 10-year term under President Bush and President Obama and was seen as so important to the national security of the country that President Obama asked him to stay on,
sentences.zh: 他在布什总统和奥巴马总统任内完成了完整的10年任期，并且被认为对国家安全至关重要，以至于奥巴马总统请求他留任，

sentences.en: in fact, after the 10 years had never been done before.
sentences.zh: 事实上，这在10年任期结束后是前所未有的。

sentences.en: But the thing to know about Bob Mueller is we can't really talk about Bob Mueller without talking about the red car.
sentences.zh: 但关于鲍勃·穆勒，有一件事必须知道，如果不谈那辆红色的车，我们就无法真正谈论鲍勃·穆勒。

sentences.en: So anybody who's ever briefed Mueller has some variation of the story.
sentences.zh: 所以任何向穆勒汇报过工作的人都有这个故事的各种版本。

sentences.en: They come in and they want to explain some case to Mueller and they have somebody under surveillance.
sentences.zh: 他们进来想向穆勒解释某个案件，并且他们正在监视某个人。

sentences.en: And they say, OK, you know, we're following this car and this is the case and we've got the surveillance up.
sentences.zh: 他们说，好的，你知道，我们在跟踪这辆车，这就是案情，我们已经部署了监视。

sentences.en: And Mueller goes through the normal questions.
sentences.zh: 然后穆勒会问一些常规问题。

sentences.en: Well, what do we know about the guy?
sentences.zh: 嗯，我们对这个人了解多少？

sentences.en: What's the crime?
sentences.zh: 罪名是什么？

sentences.en: What is the evidence?
sentences.zh: 证据是什么？

sentences.en: What do we got?
sentences.zh: 我们掌握了什么？

sentences.en: And the brief is doing great.
sentences.zh: 汇报做得很好。

sentences.en: And then at the last minute, it's what color is the car?
sentences.zh: 然后在最后一刻，他会问那辆车是什么颜色的？

sentences.en: Because that's the kind of detail Mueller wants.
sentences.zh: 因为这就是穆勒想要的细节。

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: And then some variations of the story are, oh, I knew that was coming.
sentences.zh: 然后这个故事的一些版本是，哦，我早就知道他会问这个。

sentences.en: It was a red car.
sentences.zh: 那是一辆红色的车。

sentences.en: And then it's what shade of red?
sentences.zh: 然后他会问是什么深浅的红色？

sentences.en: So he's very detail oriented.
sentences.zh: 所以他非常注重细节。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: Detail oriented is a very polite way of saying what has been said in much less polite ways by briefers at the FBI.
sentences.zh: 注重细节是一种非常客气的说法，联邦调查局的汇报人员曾用过更不客气的词来形容他。

sentences.en: Matt, we know the Trump administration wants the Russia investigation to go away.
sentences.zh: 马特，我们知道特朗普政府希望俄罗斯调查消失。

sentences.en: Is the appointment of Mueller, therefore by the administration or a member of it, an act of defiance from within the administration?
sentences.zh: 那么，由政府或其成员任命穆勒，这是否是政府内部的一种反抗行为？

sentences.en: I don't think it's an act of defiance.
sentences.zh: 我不认为这是反抗行为。

sentences.en: I think it's an act intended to right the ship.
sentences.zh: 我认为这是旨在拨乱反正的行为。

sentences.en: I mean, this is going to be well received inside the FBI, I'm sure, because the FBI has been sort of under siege here.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，这在联邦调查局内部肯定会受到欢迎，因为联邦调查局一直处于被围攻的状态。

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: The president has openly criticized our investigation.
sentences.zh: 总统公开批评了我们的调查。

sentences.en: They've fired the FBI director.
sentences.zh: 他们解雇了联邦调查局局长。

sentences.en: And we now know that the director felt like the president was trying to get stuff shut down.
sentences.zh: 而且我们现在知道，局长觉得总统试图让调查停下来。

sentences.en: This is a move that says we're going to let this play out and we're going to follow it till the end.
sentences.zh: 这是一个表明我们要让调查继续进行，并追查到底的举动。

sentences.en: And if the president's right, if there's nothing there, you can expect Mueller will find that and we'll run it to ground.
sentences.zh: 如果总统是对的，如果那里什么都没有，你可以预期穆勒会发现这一点，我们会查个水落石出。

sentences.en: And if there is something there, you would think, given his reputation, that Mueller's going to find that, too.
sentences.zh: 如果那里确实有问题，考虑到他的声誉，你会认为穆勒也会发现这一点。

sentences.en: Matt, the man who made this appointment, Rod Rosenstein, we're going to talk about him more in just a few minutes.
sentences.zh: 马特，做出这项任命的人，罗德·罗森斯坦，我们几分钟后再详细谈谈他。

sentences.en: But this is the same man who wrote the letter that people believed helped end the career of James Comey.
sentences.zh: 但正是同一个人写了那封被认为终结了詹姆斯·科米职业生涯的信。

sentences.en: Is it surprising that the same person calling for Comey's firing in some ways is now calling for a special counsel to investigate the president's ties to Russia?
sentences.zh: 同一个呼吁解雇科米的人，现在却在某种程度上呼吁任命特别检察官来调查总统与俄罗斯的联系，这难道不令人惊讶吗？

sentences.en: Well, if anybody was going to do it, it had to be Rod.
sentences.zh: 嗯，如果非要有人这么做，那一定得是罗德。

sentences.en: I mean, the attorney general, Jeff Sessions, has recused himself.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，司法部长杰夫·塞申斯已经回避了此案。

sentences.en: Everything falls on Rod Rosenstein's shoulders on this.
sentences.zh: 所有的一切都落在了罗德·罗森斯坦的肩上。

sentences.en: So this was his call.
sentences.zh: 所以这是他的决定。

sentences.en: And I think the pressure was was pretty intense.
sentences.zh: 而且我认为当时的压力非常大。

sentences.en: And and so that's why you saw Rod Rosenstein.
sentences.zh: 所以这就是你看到罗德·罗森斯坦做出决定的原因。

sentences.en: Matt, thank you very much.
sentences.zh: 马特，非常感谢你。

sentences.en: I appreciate it.
sentences.zh: 我很感激。

sentences.en: All right.
sentences.zh: 好的。

sentences.en: You're the beSt.
sentences.zh: 你是最棒的。

sentences.en: All right.
sentences.zh: 好的。

sentences.en: Bye.
sentences.zh: 再见。

sentences.en: On Wednesday night, the president responded to Rod Rosenstein's appointment of a special counsel, saying, quote, a thorough investigation will confirm what we already know.
sentences.zh: 周三晚上，总统回应了罗德·罗森斯坦任命特别检察官一事，称，引用他的话，彻底的调查将证实我们已知的事实。

sentences.en: There was no collusion between my campaign and any foreign entity.
sentences.zh: 我的竞选团队与任何外国实体之间不存在勾结。

sentences.en: I look forward to this matter concluding quickly.
sentences.zh: 我期待此事能尽快结束。

sentences.en: We'll be right back.
sentences.zh: 我们马上回来。

sentences.en: Hi, I'm Andrew Ross-Sorkin.
sentences.zh: 嗨，我是安德鲁·罗斯·索尔金。

sentences.en: I cover business and policy for DealBook, a daily newsletter at The New York Times.
sentences.zh: 我为《纽约时报》的每日通讯《交易手册》报道商业和政策新闻。

sentences.en: On November 18th, I'm going to be interviewing some of the most consequential leaders in business, politics and culture, including J.D.
sentences.zh: 11月18日，我将在纽约市举行的“交易手册峰会”上现场采访一些商业、政治和文化领域最具影响力的领导人，包括J.D.

sentences.en: Vance, Elon Musk, Christine Lagarde, Zilran Mondani and many others live on stage at the DealBook Summit in New York City.
sentences.zh: 万斯、埃隆·马斯克、克里斯蒂娜·拉加德、齐尔兰·蒙达尼等等。

sentences.en: You can watch some of these unguarded, unfiltered conversations as they happen.
sentences.zh: 你可以观看其中一些毫无保留、未经剪辑的对话实况。

sentences.en: We're going to be live streaming select interviews for anyone to watch free at NYTimes.com on November 18th.
sentences.zh: 我们将在11月18日通过NYTimes.com免费直播部分精选采访，供所有人观看。

sentences.en: If you're not already a subscriber, you can download The New York Times app to watch and get a month of free access to all of our journalism.
sentences.zh: 如果你还不是订阅用户，可以下载《纽约时报》应用程序观看，并获得我们所有新闻报道一个月的免费访问权限。

sentences.en: I hope you'll tune in.
sentences.zh: 希望你能收看。

sentences.en: You won't want to miss it.
sentences.zh: 你一定不想错过。

sentences.en: A key figure in all of this is the new deputy attorney general, the second in command at the Justice Department.
sentences.zh: 这一切中的关键人物是新任副司法部长，司法部的二号人物。

sentences.en: A very important figure is about to emerge and he's somebody most Americans have never even heard of.
sentences.zh: 一个非常重要的人物即将出现，而他是一个大多数美国人甚至从未听说过的人。

sentences.en: The man who would take over the investigation is at the center of the storm.
sentences.zh: 那个将接手调查的人正处于风暴中心。

sentences.en: His name is Rod Rosenstein.
sentences.zh: 他的名字叫罗德·罗森斯坦。

sentences.en: Rod Rosenstein.
sentences.zh: 罗德·罗森斯坦。

sentences.en: Rod Rosenstein.
sentences.zh: 罗德·罗森斯坦。

sentences.en: Rod Rosenstein.
sentences.zh: 罗德·罗森斯坦。

sentences.en: So who is this guy?
sentences.zh: 那么这家伙是谁？

sentences.en: Glenn, let's start with how we first heard the name Rod Rosenstein in the first place.
sentences.zh: 格伦，我们先从我们最初是怎么听到罗德·罗森斯坦这个名字开始吧。

sentences.en: Well, the first thing that happened, Michael, was that Jeff Sessions had to recuse himself from the investigation into potential Russian involvement in 2016 campaign.
sentences.zh: 嗯，迈克尔，发生的第一件事是杰夫·塞申斯不得不回避对2016年竞选活动中潜在俄罗斯干预的调查。

sentences.en: Glenn Thrush covers the White House.
sentences.zh: 格伦·思拉什负责报道白宫新闻。

sentences.en: Because he himself had previously undisclosed contacts with Russian officials.
sentences.zh: 因为他自己之前与俄罗斯官员有未披露的接触。

sentences.en: And as the number two in the department, Rosenstein was delegated to take it over.
sentences.zh: 作为司法部的二号人物，罗森斯坦被委派接手此事。

sentences.en: And he's also responsible for a broad array of oversight functions, including the FBI.
sentences.zh: 他还负责广泛的监督职能，包括联邦调查局。

sentences.en: So he is sort of the guy to do all of this.
sentences.zh: 所以他算是负责这一切的人。

sentences.en: So what happened between Rosenstein and Comey over the past few weeks?
sentences.zh: 那么过去几周罗森斯坦和科米之间发生了什么？

sentences.en: Here's a chronology as best as we know it.
sentences.zh: 这是我们所知的最佳时间线。

sentences.en: But Rosenstein, the deputy attorney general, sits with Director Comey earlier this month.
sentences.zh: 本月初，副司法部长罗森斯坦与科米局长会面。

sentences.en: And Comey asked for more resources to expand the Russia investigation.
sentences.zh: 科米要求提供更多资源以扩大俄罗斯调查。

sentences.en: Then that consequential weekend at Bedminster, New Jersey, the president with Jared Kushner, his son-in-law, essentially decides to get rid of Comey.
sentences.zh: 然后是在新泽西州贝德明斯特那个重要的周末，总统与他的女婿贾里德·库什纳基本上决定除掉科米。

sentences.en: The following Monday, we're not sure the exact circumstances, but Rosenstein is over in the White House.
sentences.zh: 接下来的周一，我们不确定具体情况，但罗森斯坦在白宫。

sentences.en: And at that point, the president pushes him to articulate his grievances against Comey.
sentences.zh: 就在那时，总统敦促他阐述对科米的不满。

sentences.en: And this is where it really gets interesting.
sentences.zh: 这就是真正有趣的地方。

sentences.en: Rosenstein hits the number 10 on the scale here.
sentences.zh: 罗森斯坦在这里把不满程度提到了最高级。

sentences.en: And he essentially lays out the case for Trump to get rid of Comey.
sentences.zh: 他基本上为特朗普除掉科米提供了理由。

sentences.en: Which he then does.
sentences.zh: 特朗普随后就这么做了。

sentences.en: Glenn, in what form did Rosenstein lay out that case?
sentences.zh: 格伦，罗森斯坦是以什么形式提出这些理由的？

sentences.en: Well, he put it down in a letter really at the president's requeSt.
sentences.zh: 嗯，他确实是在总统的要求下，把这些写进了一封信里。

sentences.en: It really articulated, I think, a lot of the concerns that Democrats and Republicans had about Comey.
sentences.zh: 我认为，这确实清晰地表达了民主党人和共和党人对科米的大量担忧。

sentences.en: But it was a very useful document for the president to have at that particular point in time.
sentences.zh: 但对于总统来说，在那个特定的时间点，这是一份非常有用的文件。

sentences.en: So I'm interested in who Rosenstein is in all of this.
sentences.zh: 所以我对罗森斯坦在这一切中所扮演的角色很感兴趣。

sentences.en: Is he a civil servant kind of thrust into a pretty extraordinary situation by chance?
sentences.zh: 他是一个偶然被推入这种极端境地的公务员吗？

sentences.en: Or is he a pretty savvy political operator?
sentences.zh: 还是一个相当精明的政治操盘手？

sentences.en: What do we know about Rosenstein before last week, before all this controversy started?
sentences.zh: 在上周之前，在所有这些争议开始之前，我们对罗森斯坦了解多少？

sentences.en: Not a lot.
sentences.zh: 了解不多。

sentences.en: He was the longest serving U.S.
sentences.zh: 他是美国任职时间最长的联邦检察官。

sentences.en: attorney in the country.
sentences.zh: （接上句）

sentences.en: He was appointed by President Bush and stayed through the Obama administration.
sentences.zh: 他由布什总统任命，并在奥巴马政府时期留任。

sentences.en: That is incredibly unusual.
sentences.zh: 这非常罕见。

sentences.en: With a Joe Friday, just the fact style has always been known for an impeccable nonpartisan reputation.
sentences.zh: 他以那种“乔·弗莱迪”式的实事求是的风格，一直以无可挑剔的无党派声誉而闻名。

sentences.en: One senator even remarked, you know, you are the answer to the times that we are living in.
sentences.zh: 一位参议员甚至评价说，你知道，你就是我们这个时代所需要的答案。

sentences.en: What do we know about why he would want to be in Donald Trump's Justice Department in the first place?
sentences.zh: 我们知道他当初为什么会想要加入唐纳德·特朗普的司法部吗？

sentences.en: Well, my sense from talking with people who knew him is that this guy really is a public servant.
sentences.zh: 嗯，根据我与认识他的人交谈后的感觉，这家伙确实是一位公仆。

sentences.en: I, like many other folks in the legal community who know Rod, were very heartened that such a sort of law and order, straight shooter,
sentences.zh: 像法律界许多认识罗德的其他同行一样，我感到非常振奋，因为这样一位讲究法治、直率、

sentences.en: non-self-aggrandizing person would be sort of running the Department of Justice in the new administration.
sentences.zh: 不自我吹嘘的人，将在新政府中掌管司法部。

sentences.en: Megan Brown met Rod Rosenstein in 2000, when he hired her in the U.S.
sentences.zh: 梅根·布朗在2000年结识了罗德·罗森斯坦，当时他聘请她在马里兰州的美国联邦检察官办公室工作。

sentences.en: attorney's office in Maryland.
sentences.zh: （接上句）

sentences.en: He's what I consider the archetype of a civil servant, that he has always encouraged me to go to government, others to go to government.
sentences.zh: 他是我心目中公务员的典范，他一直鼓励我进入政府工作，也鼓励其他人进入政府。

sentences.en: And so when he was nominated, we were all thrilled.
sentences.zh: 所以当他被提名时，我们都感到非常激动。

sentences.en: Many of us were hoping and suggesting that he should be the DAG, because he's so well regarded by prosecutors, law enforcement, both sides of the aisle.
sentences.zh: 我们许多人当时都在期待并建议由他担任副司法部长，因为他在检察官、执法部门以及两党中都备受推崇。

sentences.en: So I was really gratified that he was willing to serve.
sentences.zh: 所以我很高兴他愿意出任此职。

sentences.en: He was overwhelmingly approved, something like 94 to 6, I think.
sentences.zh: 他以压倒性优势获得批准，我想大概是94票对6票。

sentences.en: And when you talk to senators, Democratic senators, one of the reasons why he got such overwhelming support is they expected him to be a nonpartisan guardian of the department.
sentences.zh: 当你与参议员，特别是民主党参议员交谈时，他获得如此压倒性支持的原因之一，是他们期望他能成为司法部无党派的守护者。

sentences.en: And that is precisely the reason why Donald Trump decided to deploy him in this regard.
sentences.zh: 而这正是唐纳德·特朗普决定在这方面启用他的原因。

sentences.en: So it is his credibility, the fact that he was somebody who placed himself above the petty needs of politics
sentences.zh: 所以正是他的信誉，以及他是一个将自己置于政治琐碎需求之上的人，

sentences.en: to represent what the department stands for, is why he was in it in the first place.
sentences.zh: 去代表司法部的立场，这才是他最初入选的原因。

sentences.en: I want to understand that a little bit better.
sentences.zh: 我想更深入地了解这一点。

sentences.en: You're saying Trump chose to use Rosenstein's grievances against Comey and to explain Comey's firing because of Rosenstein's reputation,
sentences.zh: 你是说特朗普选择利用罗森斯坦对科米的不满，并借此解释解雇科米的原因，是因为罗森斯坦的声誉，

sentences.en: because the president thought it would look better?
sentences.zh: 因为总统认为这样看起来会更好？

sentences.en: Yeah, that's absolutely right.
sentences.zh: 是的，完全正确。

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: Remember, this is a president who has hired a lot of his key officials, including General Mattis at the Department of Defense,
sentences.zh: 记住，这位总统聘请了他的许多关键官员，包括国防部长马蒂斯将军，

sentences.en: because he has said that they, quote, come straight out of central casting.
sentences.zh: 是因为他说这些人是“从选角中心直接挑选出来的”。

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: Well, Rod Rosenstein comes straight out of central casting if you need a credible bipartisan figure to sort of stand up in this crisis and defend you.
sentences.zh: 嗯，如果你需要一个可信的、两党都能接受的人物，在危机中站出来为你辩护，罗德·罗森斯坦就是从选角中心直接走出来的最佳人选。

sentences.en: So in light of all this, let's go back to last week with the letter that Rosenstein wrote.
sentences.zh: 鉴于这一切，让我们回到上周罗森斯坦写的那封信。

sentences.en: Regardless of whether it was actually the reason President Trump fired Comey, was Rosenstein genuinely calling for James Comey's dismissal?
sentences.zh: 无论这是否真的是特朗普总统解雇科米的原因，罗森斯坦当时是否真的在呼吁罢免詹姆斯·科米？

sentences.en: Yes.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: I mean, look, he doesn't explicitly say the director needs to be fired.
sentences.zh: 我是说，你看，他并没有明确说局长必须被解雇。

sentences.en: But at the very end of the letter, he essentially says, we need a director that can do X, Y and Z.
sentences.zh: 但在信的最后，他本质上说，我们需要一位能做到某某某的局长。

sentences.en: And very clearly it is not James Comey, because in the previous thousand words of this letter has been an indictment against Comey, which uses the word wrong.
sentences.zh: 很明显那不是詹姆斯·科米，因为这封信的前一千字都是对科米的控诉，其中用到了“错误”这个词。

sentences.en: And by the way, for those of us who are used to reading legal documents, you very seldom see the word wrong.
sentences.zh: 顺便说一句，对于我们这些习惯阅读法律文件的人来说，你很少会看到“错误”这个词。

sentences.en: Rod is honest and ethical and would write something that he believes in and is not going to be bowing to any sort of pressure or expectation.
sentences.zh: 罗德诚实且有道德，他会写下他所相信的东西，并且不会向任何压力或期望低头。

sentences.en: He's going to, you know, advise the president and the attorney general honestly and fairly and do what's best in his view for the administration of justice at the department.
sentences.zh: 他会诚实、公正地向总统和司法部长提供建议，并从他的角度出发，为司法部的司法行政做出最好的决定。

sentences.en: I don't think anyone who could submit this to their boss, much less the president of the United States, would have any doubt in their mind that it would be interpreted
sentences.zh: 我不认为任何能把这份文件提交给上司，更不用说提交给美国总统的人，会怀疑它会被解读为

sentences.en: as calling for Director Comey's ouster.
sentences.zh: 是在呼吁罢免科米局长。

sentences.en: And what we have heard is that he was upset that it was used essentially as it was by the White House as the prime mover for pushing Comey out.
sentences.zh: 我们听到的是，他对这封信被白宫用作推动科米下台的主要依据感到不满。

sentences.en: That said, U.S.
sentences.zh: 话虽如此，美国联邦检察官并不以天真著称。

sentences.en: prosecutors are not known to be naive.
sentences.zh: （接上句）

sentences.en: They have remarkably attuned senses of both legal propriety and how things are going to be interpreted in the public sphere.
sentences.zh: 他们对法律的适当性以及事情在公共领域会被如何解读，有着极其敏锐的感知。

sentences.en: So the notion that Rod Rosenstein is one of the most experienced people in the Justice Department
sentences.zh: 所以，认为罗德·罗森斯坦作为司法部最有经验的人之一，

sentences.en: would not have known that this thing would have blown up, to me, strains credulity.
sentences.zh: 竟然不知道这件事会闹大，这在我看来是难以置信的。

sentences.en: Which leads me to this tricky question.
sentences.zh: 这引出了一个棘手的问题。

sentences.en: Was Rod Rosenstein used by the Trump White House in this case?
sentences.zh: 罗德·罗森斯坦在这个案件中被特朗普白宫利用了吗？

sentences.en: Was he part of the original White House plan to fire Comey?
sentences.zh: 他是白宫解雇科米最初计划的一部分吗？

sentences.en: Or was he a scapegoat for it?
sentences.zh: 还是他只是其中的替罪羊？

sentences.en: Yes.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: Look, we don't know what their intention was.
sentences.zh: 看，我们不知道他们的意图是什么。

sentences.en: We can only discern what their actions were.
sentences.zh: 我们只能通过他们的行为来判断。

sentences.en: President Trump has a history going way back to his days in New York as a developer and as a celebrity for having disposable defenders,
sentences.zh: 特朗普总统早在纽约担任开发商和名人时期，就有使用“一次性”辩护者的历史，

sentences.en: for using human shields in a public relations sense.
sentences.zh: 在公共关系意义上使用“人盾”。

sentences.en: The president has an implicit understanding with almost everyone that he hires.
sentences.zh: 总统与他雇佣的几乎每个人之间都有某种隐含的默契。

sentences.en: In exchange for his power, his influence, and in some cases his money, what they give him is a willingness to go to the wall for him.
sentences.zh: 作为对他权力、影响力和在某些情况下金钱的回报，他们给予他的是一种为他赴汤蹈火的意愿。

sentences.en: And so I think he views it as being the role, and I've gotten this from talking to dozens of folks who've worked with him over the years.
sentences.zh: 所以我认为他将其视为一种角色，我是从与多年来与他共事的数十人交谈中得出这一点的。

sentences.en: He views their role as defending him no matter what.
sentences.zh: 他认为他们的角色就是无论如何都要为他辩护。

sentences.en: And so he believes that he's fulfilled his end of the bargain by bringing these people into his universe.
sentences.zh: 所以他相信，通过将这些人带入他的圈子，他已经履行了交易中属于他的那部分。

sentences.en: And in exchange, they have to be willing to take their lumps.
sentences.zh: 作为交换，他们必须愿意承受打击。

sentences.en: But you're talking about a compact, some sort of understanding between the president and those who work with him that it seems the president understands.
sentences.zh: 但你谈论的是一种契约，一种总统与他手下之间似乎总统自己理解的某种默契。

sentences.en: The question is whether people like Rod Rosenstein understand the nature of this thing you're talking about.
sentences.zh: 问题在于，像罗德·罗森斯坦这样的人是否理解你所说的这种东西的本质。

sentences.en: And here, Michael, you are getting to the fundamental point here.
sentences.zh: 迈克尔，在这里你触及了问题的核心。

sentences.en: When you're in a private business and when you have people sign nondisclosure agreements, or you're in a campaign and people know precisely what they're signing on to,
sentences.zh: 当你在私营企业工作，让人们签署保密协议时，或者在竞选活动中，人们清楚地知道他们签署的是什么，

sentences.en: yes, absolutely.
sentences.zh: 是的，绝对是这样。

sentences.en: There's not a single person in the White House political shop or press office who doesn't understand that implicit compact.
sentences.zh: 白宫政治部门或新闻办公室里没有一个人不理解那种隐含的契约。

sentences.en: Now, when you bring in these high-ranking career public officials who have sworn their oath of allegiance not to the president of the United States,
sentences.zh: 现在，当你引入这些高级职业公职人员时，他们宣誓效忠的对象不是美国总统，

sentences.en: not to his business, not to his campaign, but to upholding the Constitution, then you start getting into situations like Rod Rosenstein.
sentences.zh: 不是他的企业，也不是他的竞选团队，而是维护宪法，那么你就会开始遇到像罗德·罗森斯坦这样的情况。

sentences.en: I suspect that unless the president changes his modus operandi, we are going to see more Rod Rosensteins.
sentences.zh: 我怀疑，除非总统改变他的行事方式，否则我们将看到更多的“罗德·罗森斯坦”。

sentences.en: What do you mean by that?
sentences.zh: 你这话是什么意思？

sentences.en: That you think maybe more public officials will be tossed under the bus by the president?
sentences.zh: 你是认为可能会有更多的公职人员被总统“抛弃”吗？

sentences.en: Not necessarily.
sentences.zh: 不一定。

sentences.en: Just people who have signed on as career officials to either serve the Constitution or serve the agency or department that they're employed by.
sentences.zh: 只是那些作为职业官员签约，要么服务于宪法，要么服务于他们所受雇的机构或部门的人。

sentences.en: I don't mean necessarily they all get thrown under the bus, but he's going to have to deal with people who have obligations to someone other than himself.
sentences.zh: 我并不是说他们都会被抛弃，但他将不得不与那些对除他之外的人负有义务的人打交道。

sentences.en: People have committed their entire careers and professional reputations to agencies, departments, or even ideas like independent jurisprudence.
sentences.zh: 人们将他们的整个职业生涯和专业声誉都投入到了机构、部门，甚至是像独立司法这样的理念中。

sentences.en: I'm confident Rod is his own man when it comes to professional matters and carrying out the duties he has assumed as deputy attorney general.
sentences.zh: 我相信罗德在专业事务以及履行他作为副司法部长的职责方面，有自己的主见。

sentences.en: And I think he takes the role of deputy attorney general very seriously.
sentences.zh: 而且我认为他非常认真地对待副司法部长这个角色。

sentences.en: It has its own obligations.
sentences.zh: 它有其自身的义务。

sentences.en: He took his own oath, and I have no doubt that he's going to do what he thinks is right
sentences.zh: 他宣誓就职，我毫不怀疑他会做他认为正确的事情，

sentences.en: and keep his own counsel and call things the way he honestly believes they need to be called,
sentences.zh: 坚持自己的判断，并按照他诚实认为需要的方式去处理事情，

sentences.en: not as a result of pressure or what other people think or trying to please other people.
sentences.zh: 而不是因为压力、他人的想法或试图取悦他人。

sentences.en: All right, Glenn, and now, of course, Rosenstein has appointed a special counsel.
sentences.zh: 好的，格伦，当然，现在罗森斯坦已经任命了一位特别检察官。

sentences.en: What does that tell us about his role now?
sentences.zh: 这告诉我们他现在的角色是什么？

sentences.en: I think it speaks to the fact that he recognizes that people in both parties are questioning his capacity and the capacity, I think, of the Department of Justice in general
sentences.zh: 我认为这说明他认识到两党人士都在质疑他的能力，以及我认为司法部整体的能力，

sentences.en: to conduct an impartial investigation.
sentences.zh: 去进行一场公正的调查。

sentences.en: And this doesn't feel like it's part of that contract we've been talking about with President Trump.
sentences.zh: 而且这感觉不像是我们一直在谈论的与特朗普总统那种契约的一部分。

sentences.en: Having covered Trump now since his inauguration, Glenn,
sentences.zh: 格伦，自特朗普就职以来你一直报道他，

sentences.en: how do you think he will react to one of his own senior officials appointing an independent counsel to investigate the president?
sentences.zh: 你认为他会如何应对他的一位高级官员任命独立检察官来调查总统本人？

sentences.en: You know, that's a great question.
sentences.zh: 你知道，这是一个很好的问题。

sentences.en: I think two months ago, Donald Trump would have maybe fired him.
sentences.zh: 我想两个月前，唐纳德·特朗普可能已经解雇他了。

sentences.en: But I think the James Comey experience and the fact that he's gotten so much blowback on this stuff
sentences.zh: 但我认为詹姆斯·科米的经历，以及他在这件事上受到了如此多的反弹，

sentences.en: and his leverage is so decreased and the support that he's getting from Republicans on Capitol Hill is faltering by the day.
sentences.zh: 他的筹码大大减少，而且他在国会山从共和党人那里获得的支持也在日益动摇。

sentences.en: I don't know.
sentences.zh: 我不知道。

sentences.en: The question is, will Donald Trump continue to react in the same way, impulsively, with political violence, right,
sentences.zh: 问题是，当唐纳德·特朗普自己的执行能力减弱时，他还会继续以同样的方式，冲动地、带有政治暴力地做出反应吗？

sentences.en: when his own capacity to execute is diminished?
sentences.zh: （接上句）

sentences.en: Glenn, finally, what do you think of the timing of Rosenstein's decision to appoint a special counsel now?
sentences.zh: 格伦，最后，你如何看待罗森斯坦现在决定任命特别检察官的时机？

sentences.en: I think it speaks to his sense of self-preservation.
sentences.zh: 我认为这说明了他的自我保护意识。

sentences.en: It was very, very clear ahead of his testimony that he wanted to present the committees and the American people with a more credible investigator
sentences.zh: 在作证之前，他非常非常清楚地表明，他想向委员会和美国人民展示一位更可信的调查员，

sentences.en: that would be perceived as being outside the political process.
sentences.zh: 一个会被认为处于政治进程之外的人。

sentences.en: I think this is a classic PR move, right?
sentences.zh: 我认为这是一个经典的公关手段，对吧？

sentences.en: You make a big announcement so that you take the pressure off of yourself.
sentences.zh: 你发布一个重大公告，这样就可以减轻自己的压力。

sentences.en: So he now has an answer when he goes before Congress today.
sentences.zh: 所以他今天去国会时，已经有了答案。

sentences.en: When they say, how can you prove that you're credible?
sentences.zh: 当他们问，你怎么证明你是可信的？

sentences.en: How can you prove that you're independent?
sentences.zh: 你怎么证明你是独立的？

sentences.en: You know, he's essentially doing, with Bob Mueller, what Donald Trump was attempting to do with him.
sentences.zh: 你知道，他本质上是在用鲍勃·穆勒做唐纳德·特朗普试图对他做的事情。

sentences.en: He's using Mueller as a shield.
sentences.zh: 他在把穆勒当作盾牌。

sentences.en: Glenn, thanks a million, and I really appreciate it.
sentences.zh: 格伦，非常感谢，我真的很感激。

sentences.en: No worries, man.
sentences.zh: 别客气，伙计。

sentences.en: All right, we'll talk soon.
sentences.zh: 好的，我们很快再聊。

sentences.en: Bye.
sentences.zh: 再见。

sentences.en: Bye.
sentences.zh: 再见。

sentences.en: Here's what else you need to know about the investigations into the Trump White House.
sentences.zh: 以下是你还需要了解的关于特朗普白宫调查的其他情况。

sentences.en: The Times reports that the president hired Michael Flynn as national security advisor even after Flynn told the administration he was under investigation
sentences.zh: 《泰晤士报》报道称，总统聘请迈克尔·弗林担任国家安全顾问，即使在弗林告诉政府他正在接受调查之后，

sentences.en: for secretly working as a paid lobbyist for Turkey.
sentences.zh: 因为他秘密担任土耳其的付费游说者。

sentences.en: That decision set off a chain of events that so far includes Flynn's firing, the president's request that James Comey back down from investigating Flynn,
sentences.zh: 那个决定引发了一连串事件，到目前为止包括弗林的解雇、总统要求詹姆斯·科米停止调查弗林，

sentences.en: and now the appointment of a special counsel.
sentences.zh: 以及现在特别检察官的任命。

sentences.en: And in the Senate, the Republican-controlled Intelligence Committee has asked the FBI to turn over the memos Comey wrote about his conversations with Trump,
sentences.zh: 在参议院，共和党控制的情报委员会已要求联邦调查局交出科米关于他与特朗普谈话所写的备忘录，

sentences.en: while the Judiciary Committee is asking the White House to turn over all its documents related to Comey.
sentences.zh: 而司法委员会则要求白宫交出所有与科米相关的文件。

sentences.en: In the House, two Republicans said that if Trump tried to influence the investigation into Flynn, as Comey's memos claim, it would be grounds for impeaching the president.
sentences.zh: 在众议院，两名共和党人表示，如果特朗普试图影响对弗林的调查，正如科米的备忘录所称，那将成为弹劾总统的理由。

sentences.en: Finally,
sentences.zh: 最后，

sentences.en: Look at the way I've been treated lately, especially by the media.
sentences.zh: 看看我最近受到的对待方式，尤其是媒体的对待。

sentences.en: No politician in history,
sentences.zh: 历史上没有任何政治家，

sentences.en: and I say this with great surety, has been treated worse or more unfairly.
sentences.zh: 我非常肯定地说，受到过比我更糟糕或更不公平的对待。

sentences.en: In a commencement speech at the U.S.
sentences.zh: 周三，在美国海岸警卫队学院的毕业典礼上，

sentences.en: Coast Guard Academy on Wednesday,
sentences.zh: （接上句）

sentences.en: President Trump said he was under assault by the news media and offered advice to the graduating class.
sentences.zh: 特朗普总统说他正受到新闻媒体的攻击，并向毕业生们提供了建议。

sentences.en: You have to put your head down and fight, fight, fight.
sentences.zh: 你们必须埋头苦干，战斗，战斗，再战斗。

sentences.en: Never, ever, ever give up.
sentences.zh: 永远，永远，永远不要放弃。

sentences.en: Things will work out just fine.
sentences.zh: 一切都会好起来的。

sentences.en: That's it for The Daily.
sentences.zh: 这就是《每日新闻》的全部内容。

sentences.en: I'm Michael Barbaro.
sentences.zh: 我是迈克尔·巴巴罗。

sentences.en: See you tomorrow.
sentences.zh: 明天见。

sentences.en: For decades, the Brooklyn Democratic Party operated as a tightly controlled machine.
sentences.zh: 几十年来，布鲁克林民主党一直作为一个受到严格控制的机器运作。

sentences.en: Until this summer.
sentences.zh: 直到今年夏天。

sentences.en: When elections ushered in a bunch of self-described reformers.
sentences.zh: 当时选举迎来了一群自称改革者的人。

sentences.en: Ever since, the party has been in the grip of a bruising, chaotic, and sometimes thrilling fight.
sentences.zh: 从那以后，该党一直处于一场激烈、混乱，有时令人兴奋的斗争之中。

sentences.en: In the latest episode of Metro, with me, Sarah Koenig, stories of people trying to maintain their influence and losing control along the way.
sentences.zh: 在《地铁》的最新一集中，和我一起，莎拉·凯尼格，讲述人们试图维持影响力却在过程中失去控制的故事。

sentences.en: Metro.
sentences.zh: 《地铁》。

sentences.zh: 在任何你获取播客的地方收听。
